# Independent audit: Ball radial centering and its actual source-face use

Audited Sections 1--4 of `candidate faf22898d0dc8331`. PASS. The audit includes the primary-source scope, the boundary fixed-point argument, and the exact projected-maximum implication. It does not audit that note's separate sharpness construction in Section 5.

## 1. Exact background scope

The locally retained primary source `historical context (not an accepted premise)`, lines 272--321, states and proves Theorem 2.2 for log-concave f with f(0)>0 and p>=1. It explicitly supplies the non-even adaptation. There is no assumption that zero is a mode. Thus applying it to f(x+.) at ANY interior x is licensed. The source PDF is `klartag-ball-background.pdf`; the cited theorem occurs on printed page 5.

For the radial function a_x(u)=r integral_0^infinity t^(r-1)f(x+tu)dt, polar integration gives volume W exactly. The centroid formula has denominator (r+1)W. The scaling L_x=f(x)^(1/r)K_r(f(x+.)) is correct. Compact support and bounded density yield a uniform radial upper bound; a small interior ball with positive continuous density yields a uniform positive lower bound at an interior origin. Dominated convergence along rays makes its radial function continuous there, so the convex set is a genuine compact full-dimensional body.

## 2. The fixed point is interior

The boundary continuity proof does not presume pointwise continuity of f at its support boundary. Polar integration about the fixed limiting origin makes the exceptional boundary set null in spherical-times-dt measure away from t=0; the countable union of t>=1/l covers the needed set. Fubini and uniform boundedness therefore prove centroid-vector continuity. The same argument works in rank one with counting measure on the two directions.

For each nonzero outward support normal v at a boundary origin, all rays with v.u>=0 have zero density. An open cone into a fixed interior ball has positive radial mass and strictly negative v.u. Hence v.m(x)<0. At a projection fixed point, m(x) is in the outward normal cone. If m is nonzero, choosing v=m contradicts |m|^2<0; if m=0, any nonzero support normal contradicts the strict inequality. Thus the Brouwer fixed point is interior and m=0 there. Ordinary centroid Grunbaum transfers through the exact all-direction halfspace identity. Containing closed halfspaces then contain their parallel through-point halfspaces, so no boundary or orientation case is omitted.

## 3. Balanced caps give the projected upper bound

For the projected ordinary volume law, the density is bounded, positive and continuous on the interior of a full-dimensional compact convex support, and log-concave by Brunn--Minkowski. In full projected dimension use the indicator-density case.

If positive weights balance the selected through-p normals, every projected point z has u_i.(z-p)>=0 for some i. The through-z halfspace in that direction is contained in the critical cap at p. Thus its mass is at most the common critical mass. This proves the maximum-depth upper bound for ALL projected candidates, including the new radial center; no preservation of a preselected center is needed. Positive balance of a complete active menu follows from the usual actual-center motion, with a fixed source inball providing the uniform strict gain near the active normals and compactness providing the old gap off them. Rank-one antipodality and complete-active-span conclusions are correct.

## 4. A useful slightly more general covering consequence

Let nu be any density satisfying the radial theorem in R^r, with total mass W. Suppose finitely many nonzero normals u_i span R^r, positive weights lambda_i satisfy sum lambda_i u_i=0, and affine cap thresholds b_i obey

    sum lambda_i b_i <=0.

Then their halfspaces H_i={u_i.z>=b_i} cover all of R^r: the weighted sum of their margins is nonnegative everywhere. A Gamma_r center supplied by the radial theorem lies in at least one H_i. Therefore

    max_i nu(H_i) >= Gamma_r W.                         (1)

In particular, equality of the individual cap masses or a common intersection of their boundaries is NOT needed if every cap already has the common upper bound Q. In that case Q>=Gamma_r W. For original buffered source caps, one must check the affine threshold sum in the actual coordinates used; one must not substitute a limiting closed indicator for a retained fractional slice selection.

## 5. Exact rank-refined mass quota on an actual source face

Consider a selected sequence and one occupied SOURCE face Q from the same-separator reduction. The proved source-face rigidity gives

    K_(p,j)=y_(p,j)+l_(p,j)D_j  (p in Q intersect Z^n),

with one pointed body D_j. A critical cap at the integer relative-interior witness q has, by actual quantile interpolation, the SAME normalized pointed threshold in every one of these fibers. In the notation f_(p,j)/l_(p,j)=c_j^*, this threshold is

    u_ij.xi >= -epsilon_j c_j^* Gamma_j(u_ij).

After subsequences, epsilon_j->0, D_j->D, and the compact actual cap menu converges. Its limiting continuous normals are nonzero and positively balanced after zero limiting weights are deleted. The balance follows from the actual contact equation: the right side is epsilon_j times uniformly bounded source gradients and buffer factors. Retain any positive balanced subcircuit, of span dimension r.

Let M_Q be the limiting ORIGINAL mixed d-volume of the fibers over Q. In each cap of that subcircuit, the contribution from these source-face fibers is exactly

    M_Q |D intersect {u_i.xi>=0}|/|D|.

Each original actual cap has limiting total mass Q_crit, hence every displayed fraction is at most Q_crit/M_Q. Project D onto the span of the subcircuit. Its actual projected uniform density satisfies the radial theorem, and the balanced through-zero halfspaces cover that space. Applying (1) gives

    Q_crit >= Gamma_r M_Q.                              (2)

There is NO parity divisor in (2). All source-face fibers have the same pointed cap fraction, and their total original volume is M_Q. The formula improves the full-rank Gamma_d quota whenever a retained balanced circuit has r<d. It uses the old actual cap records, not a newly selected parameter certificate or an invented rate cap law.

The same argument by itself does not bound the cap masses of a rate-slice law: equality of the ORIGINAL cap masses does not imply equality, or a common individual upper bound, for their conditional rate captures. A global scalar stress bound on their weighted average also does not imply that individual upper bound. This is the exact application boundary of the otherwise valid radial theorem.
